geographical_area: Genoa and its immediate surroundings (urban Genoese, Liguria)
orthographic_conventions: Académia Ligùstica do Brénno 'grafia ofiçiâ': ç = [s], x = [ʒ], æ, eu, ò, ö, circumflex for long vowels, hyphenated contractions (a-o, da-a), -nn-a for velar n. Variants from other sources (cû/cù, belìn/belin/bellin) are listed in the lexicon.
description_en: Urban Genoese of Genoa, a Ligurian (Gallo-Italic) language rather than a Tuscan-type dialect. The mode is named after the famous Genoese word belin, a vulgar noun used constantly as an all-purpose exclamation and filler. First version, built from encyclopedic sources and one academic article on vulgar phraseology.
description_it: Genovese urbano di Genova, lingua ligure (gallo-italica) e non dialetto di tipo toscano. La modalità prende il nome dalla celeberrima parola belin, un termine volgare usato come intercalare e esclamazione universale. Prima versione costruita su fonti enciclopediche e un articolo accademico sulla fraseologia volgare.

identifier_word.meaning_en: Literally 'dick'; in use an all-purpose exclamation and filler (surprise, annoyance, emphasis, admiration), whose value depends on its position in the sentence and on tone.
identifier_word.meaning_it: Letteralmente 'pene'; nell'uso intercalare ed esclamazione universale (stupore, disappunto, enfasi, ammirazione), con valore che dipende da posizione e tono.
identifier_word.attestation: Described as the best-known word of Genoese by the Ligurian Wikipedia and by Autelli (GEPHRAS, Acquarone 2015 spelling); Italian Wikipedia cites Toso for its origin and notes first Genoese written attestation in 1894 and wide Ligurian/Oltregiogo/Tabarchino spread. Etymology debated (Wikizionario: from belo 'budello'; Autelli/Toso: from bello). Not exclusive to Genoa.

known_limitations: No native-speaker review. Example sentences in examples.md are AI-composed from short documented forms and may contain errors.
Verb paradigms are limited to the present, perfect and a few imperfect forms; future, conditional, imperative and progressive are not documented here and must be avoided or kept to fragments.
The source verb table (src-lij-itwiki-dialetto) is partly garbled; irregular present forms need native checking.
No documented Genoese blasphemy formula was found; blasphemy is intentionally absent (no entry flagged blasphemy, no Italian formulas imported).
Sources use different spellings; the Academy subpages (alphabet, accents) could not be read, so letter values come from Wikipedia.
Many colloquial items (mugugno, paciugo, manimàn, cianin cianin, caruggio) come only from popular web sources and are marked unverified.
The catalog alias 'belinn-a' is not attested as a Genoese form of belin (feminine belina is Spezzino); consider removing it. The catalog mode word and the Genoa association are correct.
